title: Follow-up: #38 round-2 documentation and spec corrections
description: Groups the remaining round-2 review findings from opum-ai/glyph-cli#38, all documentation or spec correctness, none behavioural today. (2) MINOR: the README impact transcript prints the old line 'unresolved: 0 of 3 call site(s) did not resolve', while src/program.ts prints 'coverage (index-wide): 3 resolved call site(s); 0 call-shaped site(s) did not resolve'; the CLI test already pins the real text. (3) MINOR: src/impact.ts's header comment and the module-scope test name still say 'one-site path', the (a1) wording that DEC-216 (a2) replaced; the code emits the full path and the test asserts a two-site path, so a reader of the file would think it violates its own ruling. (4) MINOR: ADR 0003 and the README say two machines with different installs answer identically and that a fully dirty checkout cannot influence a --ref answer, and cache.ts says the SHA and the index format 'determine the derived index'; but every outside-root path goes to ts.sys (hoisted dependency tree, parent tsconfig reached by extends, the TypeScript lib) and computeRefKey includes none of it, so a hoisted install or an edited parent tsconfig can change a cold answer while a warm cache keeps the old one. (5) NIT: posix() in snapshot.ts rewrites backslashes in git ls-tree paths, which mangles a legal POSIX filename containing a backslash so indexer.ts silently skips it; drop it on git output or make it win32-only. (6) NIT: 'in-repo node_modules is not read from disk' is absolute while the running TypeScript package's own lib directory is served from disk even inside the analyzed repo; reword. (7) NIT: README 'Paths inside the tree that it does not contain are invisible' is garbled; intended 'inside the repository'. NIT 8 (CLAUDE.md exit family) is already GCLI-16.
plan: Fix the README impact transcript to the coverage line src/program.ts actually prints.
Reword the impact.ts header comment and the module-scope test name to true depth with the full path, citing DEC-216 (a1) as amended by (a2).
Scope the ADR 0003, README and cache.ts identity claims to in-repo content, naming the outside-root host reads the ref cache key does not hash; the design arm (hashing them) stays open for opum-doc.
Make posix() win32-only so git ls-tree paths keep a legal backslash, add a ref-snapshot test, and file the remaining TypeScript normalisation limit as GCLI-30.
Fix wording 6 and 7; run lore validate/check and bun run check.
implementationNotes: Proof. posix(): reverting it to the unconditional backslash rewrite turns the new ref-snapshot test red with 'src/back/slash.ts' invented in snapshot.files; the guard makes it green and the rest of impact.test.ts stays green. Items 2, 3 and 4 are wording and are checked against the source: the README transcript now matches the emit at src/program.ts, the impact.ts header and test name say full path at true depth, and ADR/README/cache.ts scope the identity promise to in-repo content with the outside-root inputs named. Item 5's remainder is measured and filed: TypeScript normalises a backslash to a separator, so ts.createProgram has no source file for src/back\\slash.ts under either spelling (probe: symbols [], no program file containing 'back'), which is GCLI-30. bun run check green, 85 tests; lore check and lore validate --strict green; CI run 44028261185 on 8205b21 green.

DEC-183 round-1 reviewer verdict on opum-ai/glyph-cli#68 at head 04923fc48010d0ec716401036aa7ba6ff0a25d00, reviewer model claude-opus-5-5 (read-only unit, no shell, ran nothing). Recorded verbatim:

VERDICT: REQUEST CHANGES

Review of opum-ai/glyph-cli#68 at 04923fc (GCLI-19 items 2-7). The README transcript, the impact.ts wording, posix() and the new test are correct. Two items the record calls done are only partly done: item 4 (the identity promise) and item 6 (the node_modules sentence).

Findings

1. BLOCKING — Item 6 (the node_modules wording) was not reworded, but the record says it was. The sentence the finding named is still in the tree word for word:
   - README.md:205: "**In-repo `node_modules` is not read from disk either**"
   - docs/adr/0003-...md:131: "In-repo `node_modules` is never read in `--ref` mode"
   - src/snapshot.ts:14: "In-repo `node_modules` is **not** read from disk"

   Meanwhile isTypeScriptLibrary (src/snapshot.ts:86-89, used at :136, :142, :152, :156, :174) serves the running TypeScript lib from disk even when it sits inside the repository, for example in-repo node_modules/typescript/lib when glyph indexes its own checkout. What the PR actually changed: it deleted the old README line "Only paths outside the repository root are read from disk". The new README paragraph (README.md:211-213) lists the TypeScript library only as an input that "lives outside the commit". It never says the library is read from disk inside the repository root. The ADR :89 bullet and the snapshot.ts header (:26-28) were already qualified before this PR; README:205 and ADR:131 were not and still aren't. ADR:26 states the DEC-216 (a2) ruling, so leave it alone.

   Fix: qualify README:205 and ADR:131, for example "apart from the running TypeScript package's own lib directory". Otherwise GCLI-19's finalSummary ("the node_modules ... wordings are fixed") overstates what was delivered.

2. BLOCKING — Item 4's scoping is incomplete: the unscoped identity claim survives in two places.
   - (a) src/snapshot.ts:17-19, in a file this PR edits: "That keeps the answer exact — two machines with different installs cannot answer the same `--ref` differently". This is the exact claim item 4 targeted. A hoisted install is a different install, and it does move the answer.
   - (b) docs/adr/0003-...md:92-93 now says "every in-repo answer exact across machines with different installs", while :140-142 says hosts with different outside-root inputs can answer differently. The ADR contradicts itself. "In-repo answer" is also undefined: a call between two in-repo symbols, on a value typed by a hoisted package, resolves differently depending on the hoisted install.

   Fix: scope both to "different in-repo installs", or point to the Consequences bullet. The new ADR Consequences bullet and the cache.ts:61-70 comment are themselves true against computeRefKey (src/cache.ts:71-77). That function hashes only INDEX_FORMAT, the SHA and the file list, so a warm entry does keep its old answer.

3. NIT — ADR 0003 status, docs/adr/0003-...md:101-103 (the old "two machines ... answer the same --ref identically" text) and :137-143. An accepted ADR had a stated consequence retracted with no note. This repository's precedent is docs/adr/0001-...md:125, an italic "*Corrected 2026-09-29.*" paragraph saying what was wrong and what replaced it. Add a dated "*Corrected 2026-11-17 (GCLI-19).*" note to 0003.

4. NIT — The list of unhashed inputs is partial. src/cache.ts:63-65 and ADR:137-140 name "the TypeScript library" / "library directory". The running TypeScript compiler's version, meaning the checker's behaviour and not just the lib .d.ts files, is also unhashed. So is Glyph's indexer logic beyond INDEX_FORMAT. README:213 ("the TypeScript install differs") covers the first. The ADR and cache.ts do not.

5. NIT — test/impact.test.ts:275 is posix-only and has no guard. On win32, makeScratchRepo's join (test/helpers.ts:18) turns "src/back\\slash.ts" into a directory, so the test fails there. CI is Linux-only, so this is latent. Consider test.skipIf(process.platform === "win32").

6. NIT — The posix() comment (src/snapshot.ts:60-66) says a git ls-tree path "must not be rewritten". On win32 it still is, at sourceFilesAtRef:104 and snapshotAtRef:124. That is harmless, because win32 cannot hold such a file and the key and the snapshot stay consistent, but the comment reads as unconditional.

7. NIT — GCLI-19 ties to GCLI-30 only in prose. GCLI-30's dependencies and references are empty.

Verified
- The README transcript (README.md:64-69) matches the emitter line by line:
  - header at src/program.ts:369
  - depth rows at :376 with pathLabel :157-161
  - coverage line at :386
  - indexLine at :131-133
- impact.ts:22-26's new header matches the code: edges = [edge, ...current.edges] gives the full path, and the module caller is never expanded (:209-215). The renamed test (test/impact.test.ts:145-165) asserts a two-edge path at depth 2. ADR:22-25 and :77-81 agree.
- posix() callers: repositoryPath (:73), sourceFilesAtRef (:104) and snapshotAtRef (:124).
  - On posix, relative() already yields "/", so dropping the rewrite changes nothing for host paths. listTree uses -z (src/git.ts:87-90), so a backslash arrives unquoted.
  - On win32 the rewrite is unchanged, matching discover.ts:48-50's sep guard.
  - The key listing and the snapshot use the same function, so they still agree.
  - Nothing this PR introduces breaks either platform.
- The new test discriminates. Under the old unconditional rewrite, both toContain("src/back\\slash.ts") assertions (snapshot.files and sourceFilesAtRef) go red, and not.toContain("src/back/slash.ts") also goes red. That covers both git-output call sites.
- Splitting item 5 into GCLI-30 is honest. GCLI-19's plan, notes and finalSummary all say the symbol still doesn't enter the index. GCLI-30 is To Do with real acceptance criteria, including a test in each mode.
- Item 7: README.md:203-205 now reads "inside the repository that the tree does not contain".

What a tree read could not establish
- The red-under-revert proof, the 85-test count, bun run check, lore check and lore validate --strict, and CI run 44028261185. I could not run them; I have only the record's word.
- Behaviour on win32. No CI exercises it, and repositoryPath and isTypeScriptLibrary have win32 quirks that predate this PR.
- Whether ts.createProgram actually drops the backslash file as GCLI-30 describes.
- DEC-216 (a2)'s exact text in opum-doc. I relied on ADR 0003's account of it.

Correction to the 04923fc record, which claimed items 4 and 6 done. Both were only partly done: the absolute node_modules sentence survived at README, ADR Consequences and snapshot.ts, and the unscoped identity claim survived at snapshot.ts and contradicted the new Consequences bullet. Round 2 qualifies all four, adds a dated Correction paragraph to ADR 0003 per ADR 0001's precedent, names the TypeScript compiler version and Glyph's indexer logic beyond INDEX_FORMAT as unhashed, guards the posix-only test on Windows, makes the posix() comment conditional, and adds GCLI-19 as a reference on GCLI-30.

Findings

1. BLOCKING — ADR 0003:92-94. This sentence is new in round 2: "a module that would resolve through an in-repo install is unresolved everywhere". That is a cross-machine claim, and the code does not back it.
   - TypeScript module resolution checks every ancestor's node_modules.
   - For root/node_modules, snapshot.ts:143-158 returns false (unless the directory is tracked).
   - For ../node_modules, repositoryPath returns null (:80), so the read goes to ts.sys (:138, :145, :151).
   - So on a host with a hoisted copy above the root, the same module resolves. The next sentence (:95-96) and :146-148 both say outside-root inputs can move the answer, which contradicts "everywhere".
   - Same class as round-1 #2(b). Fix: "is not resolved through that install on any machine", or drop "everywhere".

2. BLOCKING — the identity scoping still treats the TypeScript lib directory as outside the root, which is false against isTypeScriptLibrary (snapshot.ts:89-94, used at :141, :147, :157, :161, :179).
   - ADR:140-143 lists "the running TypeScript package's library directory" among "the paths outside it".
   - ADR:149-150: "Inside the root the tree, and the tsconfig the tree carries, determine the answer".
   - That is false whenever the running TypeScript sits inside the analyzed checkout. This is the common case where glyph is a devDependency of the analyzed repo, and also when glyph indexes itself: that lib is then read from disk inside the root and is not hashed.
   - It contradicts the round-2 text in the same ADR: :101-103 and :133-134 ("apart from the running TypeScript package's own library directory").
   - The same misplacement appears in three more places: cache.ts:63-64 ("host files Glyph reads outside the repository root — … the TypeScript library"), the correction paragraph at ADR:155-156 ("an outside-root input — … the TypeScript package"), and README:215-216 ("scoped to the repository root: the commit's tree and its own tsconfig determine an in-repo answer").
   - README:212-214 is correct: it says "outside the commit".
   - The record says the promise is scoped "to what the commit carries". That is the true scope, but the ADR, README and cache.ts still say "the repository root".
   - Round 1 passed the Consequences bullet against computeRefKey, but did not check it against isTypeScriptLibrary, so this is a newly caught issue, not a regression.
   - Minimal fix: scope to "what the commit carries" rather than "the repository root", or add "apart from the TypeScript library directory, wherever it sits" to ADR:149-150, README:216 and cache.ts:62-64, and stop describing it as an outside-root path.

3. NIT — ADR 0003:151, the correction paragraph's form.
   - The content follows ADR 0001:125: an italic dated lead, what was wrong, and what replaced it.
   - The placement does not. There is no blank line between :150 and :151, so under CommonMark "*Corrected…" is a lazy continuation and renders inside the identity bullet's paragraph. The blank line at :160 then makes the rest of the Consequences list loose.
   - ADR 0001's correction is a standalone paragraph, with a blank line at :124.
   - Fix: add a blank line before it, ideally moving it after the list ends (after :168).

4. NIT — GCLI-19 finalSummary overstates where the new unhashed inputs are named. It says "ADR 0003, the README, cache.ts and snapshot.ts … naming … the TypeScript compiler version and Glyph's indexer logic beyond INDEX_FORMAT as unhashed".
   - The ADR (:143-146) and cache.ts (:66-68) name both.
   - The README names "the TypeScript install" but not the indexer logic.
   - snapshot.ts names "a different TypeScript package" and not the indexer logic.

5. NIT — ADR 0003:95-99 now points to Consequences twice in a row: "Inputs the host supplies from outside the root can still move a cold answer; see Consequences" and "Inputs outside the repository root are host reads the key cannot see either — see the scoping…". ## Round-3 findings

1. Round-3 #1 ("resolves to nothing") is FIXED.
   - "is not resolved through that install" now appears at ADR:91-92, README:208-209 and snapshot.ts:16-18. "resolves to nothing" no longer appears in any of them, and the GCLI-19 record now describes what the tree carries.

     - `entries` is filled only from `files`, the tree's own sources (indexer.ts:233-239).
     - A callee declared in a hoisted .d.ts therefore maps to null in firstMappedDeclaration, which runs `unresolved += 1` (indexer.ts:180, :192-193).
   - The running TS package's own module behaves the same way. For `import "typescript"` from an in-root install, package.json sits outside the lib directory, so the module is not resolved through the install either. This is consistent with the "apart from the library directory" qualifier.

     - rel === null, which is ANY path outside the root (snapshot.ts:81, :139, :146, :152, :162, :180);
     - isTypeScriptLibrary, wherever the lib sits (:92-95, :142, :148, :158, :162, :180).
